text_blocks.snippet: Losartan is a prescription blood pressure medication that can cause common, mild side effects as well as rare, serious risks.
These symptoms usually improve over time as your body adjusts to the medication:

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up quickly)
Upper respiratory infections or cold-like symptoms
Mild stomach upset, diarrhea, or nausea

text_blocks.snippet: Contact a doctor immediately or seek emergency care if you experience severe reactions:

list.snippet: Angioedema: Dangerous swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, which can cause trouble breathing.
High potassium levels (Hyperkalemia): Can cause muscle weakness, confusion, or an irregular heartbeat.
Kidney injury or changes: Signs include a dramatic decrease in urination or swelling in the hands, ankles, or feet.
Severe low blood pressure (Hypotension): May cause fainting, extreme dizziness, or blurred vision.
Pregnancy risk: Losartan can cause harm or birth defects to an unborn baby and must be stopped immediately if you become pregnant.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more comprehensive details on the Mayo Clinic Losartan Guide or check the overview provided by GoodRx Health.
